subject: general
question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act added the Ninth Schedule to the Constitution of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**First Amendment Act, 1951**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ninth Schedule was added to the Constitution of India through the **First Constitutional Amendment Act of 1951**.
 
• It was created to protect legislation related to land reforms and agrarian laws from being challenged in courts on the grounds of violation of fundamental rights.
 
• The main objective of the Ninth Schedule was to ensure social justice by implementing laws that aimed at equitable distribution of land.
 
• The addition of the Ninth Schedule was done by inserting Article 31B, which provides immunity to laws listed under the schedule from judicial review.
 
• The First Amendment Act of 1951 was introduced by the then Prime Minister **Jawaharlal Nehru** and passed by Parliament to safeguard certain laws under the agenda of promoting social welfare.
 
• The Ninth Schedule originally contained 13 laws when it was enacted, and additional laws have been added over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Seventeenth Amendment Act, 1964:**

 
 
• This amendment further expanded the Ninth Schedule by including 44 additional laws related to land reforms.
 
• It also amended Article 31A of the Constitution to broaden the scope of agrarian reforms and ensure protection of such laws from judicial scrutiny.
 
 
 
• **Twenty-ninth Amendment Act, 1972:**
 
 
• This amendment included two Kerala Land Reform Acts in the Ninth Schedule.
 
• The aim was to ensure that these land reforms laws were implemented without legal challenges under fundamental rights.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Amendment Act, 1955:**
 
 
• This amendment dealt with property rights and aimed at limiting the right to compensation for property acquisition.
 
• It was not directly related to the addition of the Ninth Schedule but focused on addressing issues pertaining to property laws.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ninth Schedule Overview:**

 
 
• The Ninth Schedule is a unique provision under the Indian Constitution that protects certain laws from judicial review.
 
• Over time, debates have arisen about the scope of judicial review and the possibility of misuse of the Ninth Schedule.
 
• In the landmark judgment of **I.R. Coelho vs. State of Tamil Nadu (2007)**, the Supreme Court ruled that laws placed under the Ninth Schedule after April 24, 1973, are open to judicial review if they violate the basic structure of the Constitution.
